doc.title: Ralph Emerson Brown and Jasper Taylor Interview, 1961-05-23
doc.interviewee: Ralph Emerson Brown and Jasper Taylor

title: Writing Stockyard Strut and the Keppard record date
summary: Jasper Taylor tells how he wrote Stockyard Strut on xylophone, got Freddie Keppard to record it for Ink Williams, and who rehearsed in the band.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Did the New Orleans men impress you with their improvisation? Because they worked more as improvisational musicians, didn't they then?
Yeah, they did. I'm going to tell people. When did you write Stockyard? While you were at the theater?

Yeah. And you'd work it out as a xylophone solo to start with? Yeah. Oh yeah. Yeah. I'd make up the, that's where I write a lot of numbers for the, the washboard band. I'd, uh, a lot of them on xylophone, yeah. Yeah. Yeah. I'd make up the, that's where I write a lot of numbers for the, the washboard band. I'd, uh, a lot of them on xylophone, yeah.

Yeah. I'd start with xylophone. Was Freddie working with you at the theater? No. I, uh, cutting Freddie about, uh, we, uh, dear And so I came along with him and so I used to drink with him and so Freddie would always say, I'm going to make a record with you. And I told him about this number I had. And so he asked. He said, well the first chance I get is we'll make that number. And I think that I got the date to Inc. Williams. I told Freddie about it and Freddie got the band together. And we rehearsed it up and through. I don't recall why we made it but we rehearsed, I remember rehearsing at Freddie's hand. I remember Vincent was in there. Vincent was from there and play with the band. And Camel on piano. And I can't tell. I think the Dodds brothers are playing
there. I'm not sure. And Jackson, Benjo, Charlie Jackson. Because he does the Salty Dog on
there. Oh yeah. I don't know whether, I couldn't say Jackson with Freddie. Freddie was from there. Jackson didn't even need music.
There was a story about Freddie not wanting to record. Was that true? Because people would
copy his style? Oh, that could have been true. But he didn't, he wasn't so particular about recording. Well he liked me very much and so it was easy for me to get into recording.
